To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the calcineurine inhibitor cyclosporin and the calcineurinine inhibitor tacrolimus impair beta‐cell function in INS‐1 E cells.

the calcineurine inhibitor cyclosporine A (CsA) inhibits the insulin secretion in INS‐1 cells and in human islets, and the inhibition of the insulin secretion in human islets is associated with impaired insulin gene expression.
cyclosporin A (CsA) impairs insulin secretion and transcription in insulinoma INS-1E cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of cyclosporin A on the insulin‐secreting β‐cells of the pancreas.
the effect of cyclosporin and Tac on insulin gene expression and insulin secretion in beta‐cells.
the effects of the immunosuppressive drugs CsA and Tac on the insulin‐secreting beta‐cell line INS‐1E.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cyclosporine and tacrolimus are both effective immunosuppressive drugs that are used to prevent rejection of transplanted organs.
CsA and Tac impair insulin secretion and gene expression in INS‐1 beta‐cells.

cyclosporin and/or tacrolimus should be avoided in all cases of diabetes mellitus, and that the use of these drugs should be limited to those patients with a life-threatening illness, and in whom there is absolutely no other alternative.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CsA and Tac impair insulin secretion in INS‐1 cells, and that CsA, but not Tac, inhibits transcription of the insulin gene in INS‐1 beta‐cells.
CsA and Tac are toxic to beta‐cells and that the toxic effects are mediated by calcineurin.

the use of CsA and Tac in the treatment of type 1 diabetes is not recommended, but that further studies are required to determine the effects of these agents on beta‐cell function and insulin secretion in type 2 diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of calcineurin antagonists should be avoided in patients with a high risk of developing NODAT.
cyclosporine and tacrolimus are both effective in the prevention of acute rejection.
the calcineurins are a family of enzymes that play a critical role in many important processes in the body.
